‘Do not search Amazon’: Meta’s Muse now shops elsewhere by default

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (661 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 2:36 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 9:45 am.
  • Two months after Amazon slammed the door on Muse, the AI agent has stopped knocking.
  • It has been revealed that the shopping skill that guides Muse, Meta’s personal AI agent, now tells it to “leave out Amazon unless the user asks for it,” according to the instructions Muse provides when asked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 2:36 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 9:45 am.

Two months after Amazon slammed the door on Muse, the AI agent has stopped knocking.

It has been revealed that the shopping skill that guides Muse, Meta’s personal AI agent, now tells it to “leave out Amazon unless the user asks for it,” according to the instructions Muse provides when asked. The instructions include a template brief for Muse’s browser that says, “Do not search Amazon.”.

It has been revealed that the change was spotted last week by Juozas Kaziukenas, founder of the e-commerce research firm Marketplace Pulse, who asked Muse for the text of its shopping skill and compared it with the version from the day before. He posted the before-and-after on Friday. GeekWire asked Muse for its shopping skill and got the same language.

“Amazon blocked Muse, so now Muse blocked Amazon,” Kaziukenas wrote on X.

Muse is also told not to name Amazon as a site to search in that browser brief, “even as an example,” unless the user asked for Amazon. The skill steers the agent to Walmart and Target for general goods, Best Buy for electronics, and Home Depot or Lowe’s for home improvement.

Sources indicate that for Muse users, not much changes in practice. Amazon began blocking Muse in September, less than two weeks after Meta released the agent, showing anyone who tried to shop through it a message saying continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon’s Conditions of Use. Kaziukenas remarked any Amazon search would fail anyway because of the block.

In a recent development, what’s fresh is that Meta appears to be going along with what Amazon asked for. When it began blocking Muse, Amazon mentioned it had asked Meta to “remove Amazon from the experience.” Meta hadn’t said publicly how it would respond.

Industry observers note that meta didn’t respond to an inquiry about the change. An Amazon spokesperson remarked the tech giant had nothing to share.

According to recent reports, amazon objected that Muse didn’t identify itself when it browsed the site and appeared to capture and store customer credentials. Meta has remarked Muse has no visibility into people’s passwords or payment methods. The standoff set off a broader debate over who owns the customer relationship when an AI agent does the buying.

Industry observers note that since then, both sides have kept moving. More than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada signed up for Muse in its first six weeks, Forbes reported, and Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora and Wayfair are among the retailers working with Meta on it.

Industry observers note that the business stakes are high for Amazon. It generated more than $68 billion in advertising revenue last year, including sponsored products that appear as people browse its pages — ads a shopper might never see if an outside agent does the searching. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has said Muse will take a small cut of the transactions it handles.

According to recent reports, amazon has fought this battle before, suing Perplexity last November over the shopping agent in its Comet browser. It’s now pressing that case in part on the same Conditions of Use it cited in blocking Muse.

On Amazon’s earnings call last month, CEO Andy Jassy remarked outside shopping agents aren’t making a meaningful dent in Amazon’s advertising business. “Few customers are doing much shopping this way yet,” he said, adding that the experience still isn’t great or more convenient than going straight to a retailer.

Industry observers note that jassy said Amazon expects to work with “horizontal agents,” general-purpose assistants like Muse, but believes its own Alexa for Shopping will be the main agent people use to shop Amazon. Amazon debuted Alexa for Shopping in May, combining its Rufus shopping chatbot with the Alexa+ assistant.

It has since started letting some customers text Alexa to shop, much as people do with Muse.

ZetaChain's 55M ZETA Burn Isn't a One-Time Event: What Proposal 2 Really Does

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1335 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that zetaChain's Governance Proposal 2 would halt its L1 around Dec 9, mint ZETA 1:1 on Solana and burn about 55M ZETA in monthly installments.
  • According to recent reports, headlines are calling it a 55 million ZETA burn.
  • Sources indicate that zetaChain published Governance Proposal 2 on November 4, and its announcement post lays out the mechanics.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

It has been revealed that zetaChain's Governance Proposal 2 would halt its L1 around Dec 9, mint ZETA 1:1 on Solana and burn about 55M ZETA in monthly installments. Voting closes Nov 7.

According to recent reports, headlines are calling it a 55 million ZETA burn. Read the proposal's own schedule, though, and nothing close to 55 million disappears on the day the chain halts. The figure is real, but it arrives in twelve installments over 2027.

Sources indicate that zetaChain published Governance Proposal 2 on November 4, and its announcement post lays out the mechanics. About 55 million ZETA of undistributed validator emissions will be burned monthly through 2027, following the schedule on which they would have been emitted. The roadmap in the same post puts the pace at twelve monthly burns of roughly 4.6 million ZETA each, from January to December 2027.

According to recent reports, that detail changes how the number should be read. Most of the early flash coverage collapsed it into a single burn, which implies an immediate supply shock. The staged schedule tells a different story. These tokens were never going to circulate, because they are validator rewards for an L1 that is about to stop. Burning them on the original emission timetable keeps the published release schedule intact and introduces no new mechanism, as ZetaChain's FAQ puts it.

Recent findings suggest that governance Proposal 2 builds on Proposal 68, which approved the move to Solana in September with 99.4% in favor. Proposal 2 supplies the mechanics. Voting runs 72 hours and closes on November 7, and ZetaChain states nothing moves unless it passes.

If it does pass, every ZETA balance is recorded at snapshot block 20,755,000, expected around December 9. The ZetaChain L1 halts at that same height and isn't restarted. Claims open the same day through the ZetaHub migration portal, and ZetaChain's latest private AI app, ZetaLabs, releases alongside it.

The proposal also pairs the migration with a newly introduced whitepaper, which ZetaChain calls the document of record for the token after the move.

In a recent development, the snapshot goes well beyond a simple wallet count. It records liquid, staked, unbonding and unclaimed-reward balances. Staked ZETA is credited automatically, so nobody has to unstake, and exchange balances convert without any action from holders. Staking rewards stop at the snapshot height.

Industry observers note that holders who want to claim directly face a short process. They connect the wallet that held ZETA, sign a message naming a Solana wallet, and receive the full balance shortly afterward. The claim costs no fee and requires no SOL. According to the post, the portal asks only for a signature, never for a transaction or a seed phrase. A minimum of 10 ZETA at the snapshot is needed to claim.

Two edge cases deserve attention. First, ZETA wrapped or sitting in pools and contracts can't be claimed by a key, so holders need to unwrap and exit before the snapshot. Second, assets still held as ZRC-20 tokens at the snapshot can be claimed back on their original chain through a separate bridged-assets page, with a $5 minimum per token. Both are the kind of detail that catches people out when a deadline arrives.

In a recent development, on Solana, ZETA becomes a native SPL token under the same ticker, with 9 decimals and no freeze authority. The full snapshot total is minted before the portal opens, and then the mint authority is revoked, so no one can ever mint more. No third-party bridge is involved.

That sequence is the strongest holder protection in the plan, and it is also the part that can be checked in public. The supply stays capped at 2.1 billion less whatever has been burned, and ZetaChain indicates it will publish the SPL mint address and the migration program address before December 9. Once those exist, anyone can compare the minted total against the snapshot and confirm that the authority was actually revoked. That confirmation deserves the most scrutiny.

Meanwhile, the portal and its program are under independent review by Hacken, and ZetaChain indicates the portal opens only after the review is complete and the report is published. The ERC-20 version of ZETA on Ethereum is unaffected by the proposal. Purchaser and core contributor vesting completes on January 1, 2027, and ZetaChain says no newly released ZETA will be sold in 2027.

Sources indicate that the biggest practical risk is inattention. Most holders don't need to do anything until December 9, but exchange users depend on each exchange's own conversion window, and anyone holding ZETA through a contract or pool has homework to do beforehand.

Scams add another layer of risk. Any migration with a claim portal invites imitators, and ZetaChain tells holders to trust only its official domains and social accounts. A simple rule of thumb helps here: a site that asks for a seed phrase should be closed immediately, since the legitimate flow only needs a message signature.

On the technical side, claims are checked against the published snapshot rather than the live chain, so they continue to work after the halt. ZetaChain says it will announce any change to the process in advance.

Sources indicate that the vote decides the terms, not the direction. If Proposal 2 fails, the direction approved in Proposal 68 stands and ZetaChain returns with a revised proposal. Nothing moves on these terms.

Industry observers note that if it passes, the sequence is clear. The security report, mint address and migration program address arrive before December 9. The snapshot, halt, mint and portal opening follow on the day, and the monthly burns run through 2027. ZetaLabs then adds a Premium tier in the first quarter of 2027, with ZETA as the token for access and payment.

Recent findings suggest that taken together, this looks more like a retirement initiative for an L1 than a dramatic supply event. The burn is gradual, the mint is capped, and the claim process is simple on paper. Execution is what will matter most: the audit report, the published addresses and the clean revocation of mint authority. Those are the items to watch between now and December 9.

Industry observers note that ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has noted that crypto needs some of the features that made housing a safe investment for earlier generations. "We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets," Buterin wrote in a post on X on Nov. 18.

The post came a day after economist Peter Tulip published his own post on housing in Raleigh, North Carolina. According to Tulip, looser zoning rules in the city set off a construction boom and pushed real rents down 15% between 2022 and 2025.

In his post, Buterin first pointed to a benefit of young people putting their savings into stocks and crypto instead of real estate.

"One benefit of younger generations investing more in stonks and other digital things instead of housing is that it reduces perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive, instead of rejoicing when prices drop as we do for all other life necessities," he wrote.

In a recent development, still, the Ethereum co-founder mentioned that housing has had one advantage over stocks and crypto. He described it as "a culture and policy-encouraged default of investing in a safe non-crazy thing that you can't easily liquidate.".

"Modern platforms encourage the opposite of this, leading to more irresponsible behavior," Buterin added.

Ether was trading at $1,808 on Wednesday.

It has been revealed that buterin has written about housing and urban planning before. He has supported the YIMBY movement for denser development in cities for several years.

According to recent reports, in 2022, Buterin argued for a land value tax. According to him, such a tax would lower the upfront cost of buying a home and discourage speculation on vacant lots.

In a recent development, in 2025, the Ethereum co-founder called the housing market a "confusing market of peculiar NFTs." According to Buterin, what is really being sold under the label of square footage is the right to live in a particular city. At the time, he also mentioned that legalizing dense development speeds up the economy and benefits even people who prefer single-family homes.

  • Snider’s note stated the sell-off “expanded this week from an AI unwind to a broader growth downgrade,” noting that the S&P 500 excluding AI had held up until this week and is now 6% below its high.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the S&P 500 closed Friday in a correction, falling 3.59% to 6,918.45 for its seventh straight loss and its longest losing streak since February 2020. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.28% and is now down more than 2% for the year. Goldman Sachs notes the index is 12% below its Oct. 6 record, and its strategists have named the three things they’d need to see before calling a bottom.

Snider’s note stated the sell-off “expanded this week from an AI unwind to a broader growth downgrade,” noting that the S&P 500 excluding AI had held up until this week and is now 6% below its high. Goldman’s AI stock basket is down 32% since Oct. 6. Cyclical stocks have lagged defensives by 5 percentage points over the past 10 days.

Sources indicate that goldman’s note was written before Friday’s rout was fully in its data. Its exhibits are priced as of Nov. 19 and its hedge fund data run through that date. So the question is whether Friday supplied what the note was looking for — the situation could be even worse in markets than it acknowledged.

Goldman said any one of the following would support a bottom and a recovery: news that raises confidence in AI earnings, a dovish Fed signal, or a big drop in investor positioning.

It has been revealed that condition 1: AI earnings. This is the one the market is trying to test. Investor Dan Niles told CNBC that a price war between Anthropic and OpenAI is hurting both, noting their combined sequential revenue growth fell from 75% in the second quarter to 48% in the third, while combined losses rose from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion. Reuters cited a valuation of about 40 times trailing sales for Anthropic. A US Bank Asset Management executive remarked the valuation “assumes years of rapid growth.” Goldman’s own outlook notes the AI outlook for 2028 and beyond “is highly uncertain.”.

Recent findings suggest that condition 2: the Fed. Futures put the odds of a December hike at about 95%, and the Fed meets Dec. 9. Goldman’s economists expect hikes in December and March, sending the federal funds rate to a peak of 4.25% to 4.5%. A dovish signal looks unlikely soon. Treasuries did rally sharply Friday as investors looked for safety, which is not the same as a Fed pivot. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said Thursday that the Fed will need to raise rates again because inflation is too high. The 10-year Treasury yield is near 5%.

Recent findings suggest that condition 3: A big drop in investor positioning. This has often marked the end of past drawdowns.

Recent findings suggest that the first condition is unsettled, to say the least. Anthropic’s historic IPO turned into a sort of referendum on the entire AI trade, an unfair weight to put on a single, albeit remarkably important, manufacturer. The company raised $93.5 billion after underwriters exercised an option, passing SpaceX’s $85.7 billion as the biggest IPO on record. The shares jumped 17% on Thursday, then gave most of it back Friday to close at $88.91, not far above the $83 IPO price. “Anthropic faded relatively promptly,” remarked Dakota Wealth’s Robert Pavlik. “I don’t think investors believe there’s something inherently wrong with the company… I think they’re just skeptical of this market.” Morgan Stanley, the underwriter tasked with stabilizing the shares, closed its support position, removing a potential pillar of support.

Industry observers note that UBS stated the debate had shifted from whether AI investment will continue to whether it can generate enough revenue and returns for shareholders. A Capital Economics economist wrote that the IPO’s success while other AI stocks fell shows the parts of the AI ecosystem “no longer move as one,” as chipmakers Nvidia, Broadcom, Micron and AMD fell roughly 12% to 14%.

According to recent reports, nvidia’s 14% fall on Friday was its worst day in almost two years. It lost 22.9% on the week and is down 47.5% since Oct. 6, a loss of $2.7 trillion in market value. Reuters reported the SEC is probing its accounting practices. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 12, and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. The VIX, Wall Street’s “Fear Gauge,” closed at 35.89, its highest in 19 months.

“It’s a meltdown right now,” said Arun Sundaram of CFRA Research. JPMorgan Asset Management’s David Kelly took the other view: “This is not a fatal illness. It’s not even the flu.”.

According to recent reports, on the third condition, Goldman’s note notes hedge funds have already cut back. Their net leverage is the lowest since April 2025. A companion report, Snider’s Hedge Fund Trend Monitor, says the most popular hedge fund longs were crowded into the AI trade and have lagged the S&P 500 by 14 percentage points over six months. That is among the worst stretches in the basket’s 20-year history. The note described the situation for hedge funds as “bruised and broadening.”.

Recent findings suggest that but Goldman’s broader Sentiment Indicator is still above average. U.S. equity mutual funds and ETFs have taken in nearly $170 billion in the fourth quarter so far. Asset managers’ net equity futures positions are in the 82nd percentile of the past 10 years. Goldman’s equity strategists estimate the AI boom has lifted S&P 500 earnings 25% above trend. Goldman Research notes AI capital spending produced “about half” of this year’s earnings growth.

According to recent reports, the Street is split on whether this is the top. Capital Economics expects further declines. Goldman’s Nov. 17 outlook, written before the drop, forecast 8,700 by the end of 2027. In the Nov. 20 note, its range runs from about 5,800 to 8,100 depending on whether investors regain confidence in earnings. From Friday’s close, that is roughly 16% downside and 17% upside. Those percentages are my math, not Goldman’s.

Sources indicate that after the 22 S&P 500 corrections since 1980, the index averaged a 4% return over the next three months. It rose in 17 of them. E*Trade’s research is less reassuring. Of the 14 times since 1983, the index first closed 10% or more below a record, five became bear markets.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:48 EST / NOVEMBER 21 2026.

In a recent development, A sovereign AI factory is only as valuable as the companies that can actually get onto it. Across Europe, publicly funded AI factories are racing to give startups and small manufacturers supercomputer-class GPUs without pushing them into lock-in or loose data handling.

In Stuttgart, the HammerHAI AI factory is taking shape around a system from Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. using Nvidia Corp. Grace Blackwell chips. The center’s pitch leans as much on people as on processors, according to Bastian Koller (pictured), managing director of the High-Performance Computing Center Stuttgart.

“It’s very important to bring them there because everybody’s talking about AI, but we focus especially on SMEs and startups,” Koller stated. “So some startups know what they want, some startups want to try and they need help and support.”.

Koller spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Amit Eyal Govrin at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how HammerHAI avoids lock-in, its pragmatic approach to sovereignty and a concierge model that pairs each customer with a consistent contact. (* Disclosure below.).

It has been revealed that industrial owners no longer want shell programming; they expect the look and feel of a hyperscaler, which raises fresh demands on security and access. The center has already worked with customers on existing systems while it waits on the newly introduced hardware, and several have produced success stories. Rather than holding onto them, it designs its services so workloads can leave, according to Koller.

Sources indicate that “The idea is to evolve the system and the services in a way that they can simply move from us to a hyperscaler or from hyperscaler back,” Koller remarked. “Because what we are doing is, we give them a boost, we push them forward.”.

That pragmatism extends to sovereignty itself. The Stuttgart center runs an ISO-certified environment with TISAX Level 3 certification for automotive work. Full independence, down to European chips, is not realistic in the near term, Koller explained.

“We cannot now say, okay, come back in 10 years when we have a sovereign processor or a sovereign GPU or something like this,” Koller noted. “We have to look for the data.”.

Efficiency is part of the equation, too. The newly introduced system doubles the performance of its 3.2-megawatt predecessor at about 700 kilowatts, and the center reuses its waste heat. The bigger lesson is human: A concierge model pairs each customer with a consistent contact, according to Koller.

“We learn more how the users are working and thinking, to be honest,” Koller said. “… We can build up a system which is highly fancy, whatever there, nobody will use it because we never thought about what the user needs.”.

TAIPEI, 22 november 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ATEN International, wereldwijd marktleider op het gebied van intelligente besturingsoplossingen, heeft de lancering aangekondigd van de ATEN KE6948A Rugged DVI-I Dual-Display KVM over IP Extender, zijn eerste industriÃ«le KVM-over-IP-extender die is ontworpen voor bedrijfskritische activiteiten in extreme omgevingen. Als onderdeel van het ATEN KVM over IP Matrix System, dat is bekroond met de Good Design Award 2026, combineert de KE6948A een robuuste constructie, maritiem gecertificeerde betrouwbaarheid en geavanceerde KVM-over-IP-technologie om veilige en betrouwbare bediening op afstand mogelijk te maken voor uiteenlopende veeleisende toepassingen.

  • According to recent reports, jeff Bezos says Nvidia should look inside the organization for its next CEO, and he doesn’t give an outsider much chance of success.
  • Industry observers note that “If you don’t bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 5:05 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 9:50 am.

According to recent reports, jeff Bezos says Nvidia should look inside the organization for its next CEO, and he doesn’t give an outsider much chance of success. The Amazon founder, now co-CEO of AI engineering startup Prometheus, made the comments Tuesday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event.

Industry observers note that “If you don’t bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider. Nvidia is too complicated,” Bezos stated. Outside CEOs at complex companies, he added, “have a vanishingly small chance of succeeding,” and he would consider hiring one “a last resort.”.

Nvidia’s board says it has no aims to bring Huang back. Harvey Jones, the longtime director named the tech giant’s first board chair last week, opened Nvidia’s earnings call Tuesday afternoon by saying the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”.

Jones said the search will include internal and external candidates, and that the board wants a permanent CEO in place swiftly but won’t rush the pick.

Sources indicate that huang, the Nvidia co-founder and CEO for 33 years, had posted a statement on X that morning offering to return. He remarked he had “made serious mistakes” in his personal life and would cooperate with the board’s independent investigation.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he wrote.

Nvidia announced Huang’s resignation last Thursday, a day after the New York Times reported that he’d had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. Days earlier, he admitted to an affair with a woman who U.S. officials believe was recruited by Chinese intelligence, according to the Wall Street Journal.

CFO Colette Kress, who spent 13 years at Microsoft earlier in her career, is interim CEO.

Two major Nvidia investors, Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management’s Gavin Baker, asked the board to leave open “the potential return of Jensen Huang.” Analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives wrote in a note Sunday that talk of a Huang comeback is “ridiculous.”.

The Amazon precedent (not really): Bezos has been through a founder handoff of his own. He turned over the Amazon CEO job in 2021 to Andy Jassy, a longtime insider who built AWS. When Semafor raised the comparison, Bezos called it a poor one, saying there has never been a more carefully planned transition.

He stated he didn’t know enough about what happened in Nvidia’s board meetings to say whether Huang should return. But he called Huang a remarkable founder who deserves “admiration and respect no matter what.”.

Industry observers note that huang himself noted in a Bloomberg interview recorded Oct. 14 that he hoped his successor was already inside the firm.

The Nvidia comments came in a wide-ranging interview. Bezos also remarked Blue Origin is using Prometheus tools on two projects, called President Trump by far the most communicative of the presidents he has worked with, and said Robert Pattinson was the clear choice to play the next James Bond after screen tests of five finalists.

Business as usual, officially: Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, including $107.6 billion from its data center business. On the call, it raised its forecast for next fiscal year’s revenue growth to about 75%, from 70%.

According to recent reports, kress didn’t mention Huang by name on the call. Asked about the leadership transition, she said customers, suppliers and employees remain behind the company, calling it “business as usual.” She ended the call with a short pep talk that finished, “We’ve got this.”.

Recent findings suggest that in case the board was wondering about one outsider in particular, Bezos is spoken for. During the Semafor interview, he described running Prometheus as “Nirvana.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • webAI's open-weight TwIL-8B posts 98.2 on MATH-500 and says it tops Gemma 4 31B.
  • It has been revealed that A model small enough to run from a roughly 5 GiB file on a CPU now claims a 98.2 on MATH-500.
  • webAI released TwIL-8B as an open-weight model on November 4, and its Hugging Face model card leads with ambitious numbers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

webAI's open-weight TwIL-8B posts 98.2 on MATH-500 and says it tops Gemma 4 31B. The card's own footnotes show why the comparison deserves a re-run.

It has been revealed that A model small enough to run from a roughly 5 GiB file on a CPU now claims a 98.2 on MATH-500. The most revealing line in its model card isn't a score, though. It's a footnote saying the competitor numbers were never re-run.

webAI released TwIL-8B as an open-weight model on November 4, and its Hugging Face model card leads with ambitious numbers. The 8.8B-parameter reasoning model is post-trained from IBM's Granite 4.2 8B using full-parameter supervised fine-tuning, followed by GRPO/DAPO reinforcement learning. A final length-aware RL stage produces the "balanced" variant, which is the default.

The card reports 98.2 on MATH-500 and 88.3 on AIME 2025. It indicates TwIL-8B posts the highest MATH-500 and LiveCodeBench scores in its comparison group, which includes Gemma 4 31B at about 3.5 times its size. That claim is worth testing, because small models that beat larger ones are exactly what open-weight people want to hear.

Industry observers note that on MATH-500, the card lists TwIL-8B at 98.2, Qwen3.5-9B at 96.6 and Gemma 4 31B at 87.9. On AIME 2025, TwIL-8B scores 88.3 against 87.1 for Gemma 4 31B. On LiveCodeBench, TwIL-8B scores 81.6 against 80.0, though that figure carries a dagger marking it as measured on the verbose variant, not the default balanced one.

Industry observers note that the card is also more candid than most. It notes TwIL-8B is not a knowledge model. GPQA Diamond comes in at 70.2, trailing Gemma 4 31B by 14.1 points, and the model also trails on MMLU-Pro and HLE. There is no safety or preference tuning beyond what Granite carries, and the license is non-commercial. That honesty makes the claims easier to weigh.

Here is where the headline gets complicated. TwIL-8B's scores come from webAI's own internal high-effort pass@1 runs. The card states that competitor scores are published figures and were not re-run.

Gemma 4 31B's 87.9 on MATH-500 comes from Red Hat's evaluation of an FP8 build, using the lighteval harness, not from Google. The card itself notes that this figure is unusually low and may reflect answer extraction. In other words, the 10.3-point gap that anchors the headline compares one team's own harness against a third party's number that the card suspects may be understated.

Recent findings suggest that none of this makes TwIL-8B's result wrong. It means the margin isn't established until both models run under the same harness, prompt and sampling settings. For reference, Google's Gemma 4 model card is the source for several of the other Gemma figures in the table.

Industry observers note that read the whole table and the picture is more balanced than the headline suggests. In the card's head-to-head summary, TwIL-8B beats Gemma 4 31B on 3 of 14 shared benchmarks and loses 11. It leads on MATH-500, LiveCodeBench and AIME 2025, but trails on AIME 2026 (88.3 against 89.2), HMMT Feb 2026 (68.2 against 77.2), GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro and IFEval.

The AIME 2025 lead is the shakiest. The card says AIME and HMMT sets have 30 to 33 problems, so one problem is worth about 3 points, and gaps of that size sit within noise. A 1.2-point margin is well under one problem, so the result is best read as a tie.

In a recent development, against the closest same-size rival, Qwen3.5-9B, the card shows the models roughly level on contest math, with TwIL-8B using fewer tokens: about 19.5k per AIME 2026 problem against 31.2k. That efficiency claim may turn out to be the more durable one.

In a recent development, the card makes replication unusually practical. The Q4_K_M balanced GGUF weighs 4.98 GiB and runs through llama.cpp, with a command given in the card. Larger Q8_0 and F16 builds exist only for the verbose variant. The model also needs a substantial generation budget, since a short limit truncates its reasoning and scores far worse. The card suggests settings around 32,768 latest tokens and a 40,960-token context.

Anyone planning a check should expect three catches. First, the card notes all its scores were measured on bf16 weights, not the GGUF builds, so a CPU run tests a slightly different artifact, and the card expects small deviations, most likely at Q4_K_M. Second, MATH-500 is 500 problems and each answer can run to tens of thousands of tokens, so CPU testing will be slow. Third, the decoding setup matters, since the card says none of its numbers use low-effort or thinking-off modes.

For a fair comparison, the same prompt, answer extraction and sampling must be applied to Gemma 4 31B too, ideally at full precision.

The card also lists contamination caveats. Its training pools were decontaminated against AIME, HMMT Feb 2025 and 2026, MATH-500, GPQA, MMLU-Pro, HLE, IFEval, IFBench and LiveCodeBench using 13-gram matching. HMMT Nov 2025 and the HumanEval, MBPP and CRUXEval suites weren't in the decontamination set. The MATH-500 and AIME results fall inside the protected group, which counts in the model's favor.

In a recent development, overall, TwIL-8B looks like a genuinely strong small model for contest math, code and instruction following, and the card is open about its weak spots. The claim to beat Gemma 4 31B is narrower than the headline suggests: a clear lead on one benchmark, a likely tie on another and a loss on most of the rest.

The useful next step is a same-harness run of both models, with the bf16 weights as a control for the GGUF build. Until independent results appear, the 98.2 is best quoted as webAI's reported figure, and the size-beating framing is better described as unproven than wrong.

Industry observers note that MEXC confirmed that its Global Card service will be discontinued on November 18, according to the exchange's announcement. The tech giant cites service adjustments by its third-party card issuer. From the deadline, existing cards can no longer be used for transactions, and new card applications are suspended.

Users have two things to take care of before the service ends.

First, the remaining card balance has to be withdrawn: the Withdraw button on the Global Card page sends the funds to the Fiat account.

Industry observers note that second, subscriptions linked to the card should be cancelled or switched to another payment method. Unfortunately for cardholders, recurring payments will most likely fail if they stay on the old card.

If there's still a balance when the service ends, MEXC will credit it to the Spot account, so users will simply receive their funds back. It's notable to keep in mind that pending card transactions need time to settle, which is why the balance snapshot comes on November 21, three days after the shutdown. The amount will be credited within three business days of the snapshot. Users do not need to take any action.

Recent findings suggest that refunds for previous card transactions will be credited to the Fiat account once MEXC receives them. Pending cashback will be credited automatically as scheduled. Elite VVIP people with zero-fee benefits will be refunded too, though the eligible fees return to their Spot accounts only before December 15.

Transaction history, card orders and cashback records stay available on the Global Card page for three months after the service ends, so it's worth saving anything needed before access ends.

In a recent development, cryptocurrency services delegate certain types of services to third parties all the time, so witnessing a similar situation is more than a possibility here. Realistically, the shutdown is somewhat inconvenient rather than dangerous, as the balances are returned automatically. For customers: stay vigilant and try not to put all your eggs in one basket.

Only 18% of Gen Z workers want to build AI skills. A Wharton professor says using AI is riskier for them

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The generation with the longest careers ahead of them appears to be the least interested in sharpening their AI skills, according to research from talent services firm Seramount released Thursday: Only 18% of Gen Z employees want to develop or improve their AI skills, compared with 36% of millennials, 46% of Gen Xers, and 43% of baby boomers.

For younger workers, using AI could come with a different set of professional risks than it does for their more experienced colleagues.

“Because younger workers haven’t had the same amount of time in their career fields to build up their standing as experts, using a technology that blurs their own contribution to their work can feel especially risky,” Jessica Reif, an assistant professor of management at the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School, told Fortune.

The survey of more than 1,800 U.S. white-collar employees at companies with at least 500 workers, conducted in June through NORC’s AmeriSpeak panel, found that 58% of Gen Z employees use AI in their current roles, compared with 60% of baby boomers, 63% of millennials, and 67% of Gen Xers. Seramount defined Gen Z as workers 29 and younger.

Recent findings suggest that that leaves a puzzle. Gen Z workers, often cast as digital natives, use AI at nearly the same rate as baby boomers but show far less interest in getting better at it.

Younger workers are considerably more concerned about what using AI might say about their own abilities.

Sources indicate that some 22% of Gen Z employees surveyed by Seramount worry that using AI could lead others to question their skills, compared with 10% of millennials and Gen Xers and just 8% of baby boomers. Only 27% of Gen Z employees feel comfortable acknowledging their use of AI for a work task, compared with between 47% and 53% of their older colleagues.

Those concerns are not entirely unfounded. In four experiments involving more than 4,400 participants, Reif, then at Duke University, and her co-authors Richard Larrick and Jack Soll found in a study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences that employees described as receiving help from AI were perceived as less competent, less diligent, and lazier than those described as receiving other forms of help or whose use of help wasn’t specified.

The stigma could also influence hiring decisions. In one experiment, managers who used AI less frequently themselves favored candidates who did not use AI, while managers who were more frequent AI customers favored candidates who used it daily.

Recent findings suggest that the penalty in those experiments held regardless of the age of the employee being evaluated. But Reif stated its consequences could be more substantial for workers who are still trying to establish themselves professionally.

“A senior employee who uses AI has a more substantial record of results that can offset doubts about their effort or ability, but an early-career employee doesn’t have that record yet so others might weight their AI use more heavily when evaluating them,” Reif mentioned.

According to recent reports, the pressure can work in the opposite direction, too. A survey of 3,001 professionals worldwide released Tuesday by the London School of Economics’ Inclusion Initiative and consulting firm Protiviti found that 48% of employees worry about being judged for not using AI enough at work, compared with 20% who worry about being judged for using it.

For workers at the beginning of their careers, that presents a dilemma: They need to demonstrate their ability to work with AI while also proving what they are capable of doing themselves.

Beyond concerns about their professional reputation, younger workers appear less convinced of the benefits of using AI in the first place.

According to recent reports, only 30% of Gen Z employees in Seramount’s survey believe AI helps them work more efficiently, compared with roughly half of their older colleagues. And 41% believe it improves the quality of their work, compared with 56% of Gen Xers.

Young people are also questioning whether the immediate benefits of AI could come at the expense of their long-term development. A survey by Gallup, the Walton Family Foundation, and GSV Ventures of 1,572 Americans aged 14 to 29, released in April, found that 80% believe using AI tools is very or somewhat likely to make learning more difficult for them in the future.

It has been revealed that among employed Gen Z respondents, 48% believe the risks of AI in the workforce outweigh its benefits, compared with 15% who believe the opposite. Some 69% place greater trust in work completed without AI than in AI-assisted work.

That skepticism, as Fortune has reported, partly reflects how poorly schools, employers, and government have prepared young people for an AI economy.

Younger employees’ attitudes toward AI may also reflect the environments in which they are being asked to use it.

Recent findings suggest that only 27% of Gen Z respondents in Seramount’s survey said their organization provides support to help them integrate AI into their work, compared with 38% of millennials and 43% of Gen Xers. Younger employees were also the least comfortable seeking help from colleagues on how to use AI tools, with only 18% saying they felt comfortable doing so, compared with 34% of baby boomers.

Seramount suggested that junior employees may also have less need for AI in their current roles or more limited access to enterprise AI tools.

The LSE and Protiviti research points to the importance of training in AI adoption across generations: 93% of employees who had received AI training used the technology at work, compared with 50% of those who had not.

In a recent development, not all research suggests young workers are being left behind on training, though. The LSE and Protiviti study found that 66% of Gen Z employees had received AI training in the past year, compared with 40% of baby boomers. That study polled professionals worldwide, while Seramount surveyed only U.S. workers.

For employers, failing to engage their youngest employees in AI adoption could create a longer-term talent development problem, echoing warnings that automating entry-level roles could cost companies their future workforce.

Industry observers note that “If Gen Z falls behind on AI, employers risk weakening their future leadership pipeline,” Diana Forster, senior director of research at Seramount, stated in a press release. She called on employers to provide clearer guidelines, training, and opportunities for young employees to practice using the technology.

Despite the challenges young workers face in embracing AI, the technological disruption could also work in their favor.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman believes that periods of rapid technological change give people at the beginning of their careers a chance to gain a competitive advantage. As AI transforms how jobs are done and opens up new business opportunities, those with fresh ideas and new skills could have an edge over more established players.

“I think you want to start your career at a time of the greatest change, when the playing field is most open,” Altman noted during an interview with Stanford’s Graduate School of Business in October, as previously reported by Fortune.

He added, “I think people with high potential, drive, ideas, a new way of looking at things, and new skills tend to do relatively well when the ground is shaking the most.”.

For workers concerned about being judged for using AI, Reif offered some advice.

“No matter their age, employees are increasingly in a position where they need to demonstrate their value above and beyond what AI can do,” Reif noted. “Employees who are proactive in communicating how AI enables them to contribute more or in ways that would not have otherwise been possible may be able to counteract some of these perceptions.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 17, 2026 at 6:15 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 11:49 am.

Washington’s biggest economic threat may be the conviction that it’s already doing everything right.

That was the pointed warning from a Technology Alliance panel Tuesday, where a conversation about talent and economic growth became a challenge to the state’s self-image as an innovation leader.

“You mentioned spicy, right?” Rob Ogburn asked, taking up the invitation to speak bluntly.

“The economy is very strong. The economy is not competitive at all,” noted Ogburn, executive director of Business and Community Services at Central Washington University.

While tech giants such as Microsoft and Amazon and sectors including aerospace and biotech are powering today’s economy, that doesn’t mean Washington is positioned to win tomorrow’s investment, develop its workforce or spread opportunity beyond its major employment centers.

Amelia Ransom, former vice president at Smartsheet and past Nordstrom leader, questioned the definition of success, arguing that future growth also depends on investing in people and businesses outside the corporate spotlight.

Recent findings suggest that “Who do we mean when we say winning? Who is it? Who are we talking about, and who are we leaving out?” Ransom stated, later adding, “We have to close the daylight between who we say we are and who we actually are.”.

It has been revealed that the panel was held in downtown Seattle and moderated by Jolenta Coleman-Bush, director of Microsoft Philanthropies. It also included Rachel Smith, president of Washington Roundtable.

Rather than simply calling for more talent and innovation, panelists examined how Washington develops the people already here, whose perspectives inform its decisions and how effectively its institutions and stakeholders work together.

Sources indicate that unification is essential. U.S. Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., led the passage of the CHIPS and Science Act in 2022 to bolster semiconductor manufacturing and innovation in AI and energy. But her home state has received just 0.3% of the funding awarded so far, Ogburn mentioned.

He argued that other states and regions were more effective at uniting to make their case for investment, showing their collective resources and the problems they could solve.

“We indicated up and said, ‘We’re competing with our neighbor, and we’re better than them.’ No investor is going to look at that and say you’re going to make the best use of my money,” Ogburn said.

Cultivate talent, don’t just recruit it. Ransom compared workforce development to a restaurant, a grocery store and a garden: recruiting ready-made workers, developing the talent already here and growing the long-term pipeline.

Industry observers note that “The middle is where we probably need to spend more time, which is at the grocery store, which means you’ve got to learn to cook,” she remarked. Her point: Invest in Washington’s existing employees, students, and businesses.

Smith wants employers to identify the high-wage, high-skill jobs they need filled so educators and businesses can coordinate strategies to prepare workers for those roles.

Recent findings suggest that fill essential information gaps. Panelists called for a clearer picture of community skills and barriers to opportunity, more voices to challenge prevailing assumptions, and closer examination of how regulations affect businesses.

It has been revealed that “We’ve gotten in this war of the rankings where everybody’s like, “No, we’re the best. No, we’re the worst.” And we we’ve got to stop doing that,” Smith remarked.

According to recent reports, the region needs data-backed insights into the reasons behind the rankings, she mentioned. Smith pointed to the recently formed Economic Development Council and its planned statewide strategy as a step toward a more coordinated approach.

Whether these efforts succeed, Ogburn said, should be judged by the communities themselves.

“And then, if you want to measure success, go back to those communities and ask them if they feel successful,” he mentioned. “Do they have agency and self-determination?”.

Cardano-based stablecoin DJED has revealed its sunset, as DJED and SHEN services will wind down on December 31, 2026, at 11:59 pm UTC.

DJED represents a crypto-backed, overcollateralized stablecoin protocol on Cardano whose US-dollar peg is maintained algorithmically against an ADA reserve (with SHEN as the reserve coin), rather than by fiat reserves.

"DJED and SHEN services will wind down at the end of December 31, 2026, at 11:59 pm UTC," a DJED-focused X account wrote.

ATTN: DJED & SHEN Holders DJED and SHEN services will wind down at the end of December 31, 2026 at 11:59pm UTC. Please redeem and convert any DJED and SHEN you hold before then. All redemptions are subject to the reserve ratio.

Industry observers note that owners are urged to redeem and convert any DJED and SHEN they hold before this deadline. Users are to redeem on the protocol and convert their DJED and SHEN back to ADA on the official Djed page. Users who hold DJED or SHEN in liquidity pools, lending markets, or other DeFi platforms are urged to withdraw those positions first, then redeem or swap.

Recent findings suggest that the Djed team noted all systems are fully operational and redemptions are now open, subject to the reserve ratio. It further added that the Djed protocol will be maintained and remain available until December 31, 2026. After this date, all remaining funds will be allocated to the outstanding DJED/SHEN holders once the wind-down is complete.

In a recent development, djed’s shutdown comes almost three years after its launch, which came in 2023. The stablecoin was officially rolled out on the Cardano mainnet on January 31, 2023, and was developed by COTI in collaboration with the Cardano ecosystem to be used on DeFi protocols on Cardano as a stable alternative to volatile cryptocurrencies.

In positive news for the Cardano ecosystem, Monument Bank Limited has launched tokenized deposits on the Midnight network, marking a milestone for the network and the decentralized finance ecosystem.

At present, Monument is the first UK bank to tokenize retail deposits on a public blockchain, offering clients a 5.2% AER fixed-term return on savings directly through its existing banking app, delivering institutional onchain finance through a familiar and user-friendly banking experience.

Up to £250 million of client deposits will be represented on Midnight in this opening phase, with deposits recorded one-to-one in sterling.

XRP Whales Buy the Dip as $127 Million Leaves Binance With Price Below $1

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (599 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zycrypto

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that XRP whales appear to be taking advantage of the price dip, withdrawing more than $127 million worth of tokens from Binance since November 10.
  • According to CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost, whale activity on Binance has shifted noticeably over the past week.
  • The trend continued on the latest day covered by the analysis, when whales withdrew approximately $21 million worth of XRP from Binance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that XRP whales appear to be taking advantage of the price dip, withdrawing more than $127 million worth of tokens from Binance since November 10. The outflows suggest that large holders are using the downturn to accumulate rather than sell as XRP trades below $1.

According to CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost, whale activity on Binance has shifted noticeably over the past week. Daily net outflows have ranged from $12 million to $33 million, indicating that large holders have increasingly moved their XRP off the exchange.

The trend continued on the latest day covered by the analysis, when whales withdrew approximately $21 million worth of XRP from Binance. Cumulatively, net withdrawals have exceeded $127 million since November 10.

Industry observers note that this marks a notable shift from earlier whale activity, which was largely dominated by transfers to Binance. Following XRP’s nearly 72% rally over several days in August, large holders increased their exchange deposits, with inflows reaching approximately $75 million as the cryptocurrency climbed back above $1.50.

Sources indicate that the trend was even stronger after XRP climbed above $3.55 in July 2025. During that period, whales regularly transferred large amounts of XRP to Binance, with daily net inflows surpassing $100 million several times and reaching nearly $270 million in a single day.

Recent findings suggest that however, whale withdrawals are not the only activity worth watching. XRP exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $19.1 million in net outflows during the week of November 9–13, contrasting institutional investment products with the movements of large on-chain holders.

Darkfost cautioned that some of the withdrawals could be internal Binance transfers rather than genuine whale accumulation. Similar activity occurred between October 29 and November 4, when the exchange replenished its reserves following a security incident, meaning not all recent outflows necessarily reflect buying activity.

Meanwhile, the decline below $1 has attracted attention from technical analysts, with some identifying the current price range as a potential long-term buying opportunity.

Analyst Crypto Patel believes XRP is approaching an crucial accumulation zone between $0.90 and $0.60. He suggested that investors could be positioning themselves for a larger recovery while market sentiment remains weak.

In a recent post on X, Crypto Patel wrote, “XRP at $1 again. Panic or Opportunity? Everyone wants to see XRP at $10+, but very few are prepared to accumulate when the market looks ugly.”.

The analyst maintained that the $1–$0.70 range represents a macro accumulation zone but warned that a confirmed breakdown below $1 could expose XRP to another 30%–40% correction.

Sources indicate that additionally, Crypto Patel maintained a bullish long-term outlook, pointing to $3.67 as a major resistance level before potential targets of $10 and $20. He also stressed the importance of accumulating during market dips rather than chasing price rallies.

Furthermore, analyst Ali Martinez has identified another important level that could determine XRP’s next major move.

In a recent development, according to the pundit, a large ascending triangle appears to have been forming on XRP’s weekly chart since 2017. With the cryptocurrency now more than 43% below its October high of $1.55, the analyst believes the ongoing correction could extend further.

Martinez pointed to the triangle’s rising trendline around $0.78 as a potential bottom, suggesting that buyers could emerge around this level to prevent further losses.

Industry observers note that if $0.78 holds, XRP could rebound toward $3.50. A weekly breakout above that resistance, followed by a successful retest, could confirm the pattern, with Martinez projecting a potential rally toward $18.

At press time, XRP was trading at $0.9, down 7.31% over the past 24 hours.

#87641. ‘An extraordinary and extreme backstop’: Earthjustice warns Army off bypassing paused Iowa permit

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1357 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fortune ↗ Open Full Page

‘An extraordinary and extreme backstop’: Earthjustice warns Army off bypassing paused Iowa permit

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1357 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fortune

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A federal appeals court has paused the emergency permit authorizing the U.S.
  • According to recent reports, in a notice filed on behalf of the Environmental Protection Agency, government lawyers said they would oppose a motion by two environmental groups to keep the permit on hold.
  • Industry observers note that the notice did not say whether the Army plans to go ahead with the detonation, now set for Monday, Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A federal appeals court has paused the emergency permit authorizing the U.S. Army to blow up nearly five tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. But the Justice Department told the court Friday that the Army may be able to proceed without it.

According to recent reports, in a notice filed on behalf of the Environmental Protection Agency, government lawyers said they would oppose a motion by two environmental groups to keep the permit on hold. The notice added that “in qualifying emergency situations,” EPA regulations authorize the Army, which is not a party to the case, “to implement waste treatment activity without an EPA permit” when there is “an immediate threat to human health, public safety, property, or the environment.”.

Industry observers note that the notice did not say whether the Army plans to go ahead with the detonation, now set for Monday, Nov. 23. An Army Sustainment Command spokesperson did not respond Friday when asked whether the Army would proceed while the stay is in place, the Iowa Capital Dispatch reported. On Friday evening, Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds activated the State Emergency Operations Center to coordinate state, federal, and local agencies ahead of the planned blast.

Thien Chau, a senior attorney at Earthjustice, which represents the groups, called the emergency provision “an extraordinary and extreme backstop” and noted the groups “strongly urge” the Army not to rely on it.

The standoff leaves residents of southeastern Iowa and western Illinois facing a weekend of uncertainty over whether a plume of lead-laden dust will drift across their towns and farmland on Monday.

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit issued its order late Thursday, pausing the permit the EPA issued to the Army on Nov. 13 after finding the material posed an “imminent and substantial endangerment to human health and the environment.” The pause lasts until the court rules on the groups’ emergency motion, which asks it to keep the permit on hold while it decides the case. The government noted it would file its full response by Sunday.

Cody Smith, director of climate initiatives at the Iowa Environmental Council, one of the groups that filed the lawsuit, stated detonating without the court’s approval would be unlawful. The council and the Sierra Club Iowa Chapter argue that the permit lacks adequate protections for health and the environment, that the EPA did not fully consider alternatives, and that it was issued without the public notice and comment they say the rules require.

Sources indicate that hours before the court acted, the Army postponed the detonation from Friday to Monday. Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said Monday was the “latest possible moment prior to a forecasted temperature drop, which would risk further destabilization of the material.”.

The 68 drums of lead azide, an explosive used to set off munitions, were stored on site for more than 20 years in a bath of ethanol and water. The Army indicates the material degraded and recrystallized, leaving it highly sensitive to friction and shock.

Recent findings suggest that the blast is expected to release a plume of dust containing lead. Army maps modeled for a Friday detonation projected the dust settling across a roughly 25-mile stretch north of the plant, with low levels of airborne lead traveling farther. The Army asked some residents of Middletown, a town of about 360, to leave their homes during the blast because it could shatter windows.

The permit required the Army to model the plume using conservative assumptions so as not to “under-predict” potential impacts, and it states that EPA and Army experts agree the modeling is “not necessarily representative of actual conditions.”.

In a recent development, the Army held a public open house about the planned detonation in mid-October. On Nov. 15, five days before the original blast date, it released the detonation date and plume maps, meeting the permit’s requirement to publish a preliminary forecast at least five days in advance.

In a recent development, smith said the council began receiving calls from concerned residents on Monday, Nov. 16, and when it contacted state and local officials, “We were telling them for the first time.” Reynolds’ office has said neither the governor nor any state agency was told of the looks before the Army’s Nov. 15 announcement, Little Village reported.

“This lawsuit is largely the outcome of a last resort,” Smith said.

A letter from the EPA paints a different picture. Writing to Reynolds on Friday, Jim Macy, who heads the EPA’s Region 7 office, remarked the agency issued three emergency permits for the lead azide between April and September and notified Iowa’s congressional delegation, state lawmakers, and local officials each time, and again on Nov. 13 when it approved the detonation.

In a recent development, illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, Illinois Sens. Dick Durbin and Tammy Duckworth, and Iowa Sen.-elect Josh Turek were among a bipartisan group of officials who wrote to Telle and EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin urging a delay. “We call on you to consider delaying this detonation until there is an opportunity to explore safer alternatives,” they wrote, according to CBS News.

The Army’s environmental assessment considered chemical neutralization, which would avoid a blast plume, but rejected it. The assessment concluded that the 7 to 22 days of handling it would require created an unacceptable risk of a fatal accidental detonation, with no guarantee that neutralization would work.

Macy’s letter mentioned the Army also weighed building a structure over the material, moving it to the plant’s open detonation unit, and leaving the drums in place, and found each posed “an unacceptable safety risk” because of “advanced crystallization.” The Army, he wrote, “concluded the only viable option was a controlled detonation in place with extensive mitigation measures.”.

The environmental groups say the Army chose detonation “without full consideration of less dangerous alternatives that would avoid widespread dispersal and deposition of toxic lead.”.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s not our role to recommend to the Army or the EPA how to deal with explosives most effectively,” Smith said. “As far as we can tell, it’s been stored on site for at least 20 years, and they’ve known about this for at least the last several months. And they decided to wait until the very last minute to concern that permit and make it publicly known.”.

Sources indicate that in September 2025, the Army posted a federal contracting notice saying it planned to have American Ordnance LLC, which operates the plant, perform “lead azide neutralization.” The notice did not describe the method. The Army’s environmental assessment notes the material’s degradation was discovered in March 2026. The Army has not responded to requests for clarification about the notice.

Army spokesperson Justine Barati told Radio Iowa on Nov. 17 that residents worried about lead dust on their property had a simple remedy: “The good thing is, if people have concerns about it being on their property, all they have to do is hose that off, and it’s gone.” The station reported that fine lead particles could reach as far north as Maquoketa.

Smith noted that advice, including the Army’s guidance to hose off playground equipment and wash cars, is inconsistent with how lead persists in the environment. The groups’ court filings called the idea that lead can be washed away “absurd, counterfactual, and extremely harmful misinformation to share with the public.” Iowa health officials say no safe level of lead exposure has been identified.

In his letter, Macy mentioned EPA staff have been in Middletown since Nov. 16 testing drinking water and watersheds, and that the EPA and Army will provide filters to homeowners on public water systems if testing finds elevated lead.

“People have really been scrambling for information about what to do,” Smith said.

The court could rule before Monday. If it grants the groups’ motion, the permit stays on hold while the case proceeds. If it denies the motion, the pause ends and the Army is free to proceed under the permit. Whether the Army would invoke the emergency exception if the court rules against it remains an open question.

Bitcoin itself recorded nearly $202 million in liquidations, with bullish traders suffering the majority of forced closures.

Industry observers note that this creates a difficult environment for buyers. Falling prices trigger liquidations, which create additional selling pressure and push prices lower. The reduction in open interest also suggests excessive leverage is being flushed from the market.

Base Switches Off Flashblocks as Denim Goes Live: The Migration Risks Behind 200ms Blocks

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1246 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that base's Denim upgrade replaced Flashblocks with five canonical blocks per second.
  • For about sixteen months, Base's fastest blocks were only promises.
  • Denim went live on Base mainnet on November 5, after activating on Sepolia on October 21.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Sources indicate that base's Denim upgrade replaced Flashblocks with five canonical blocks per second. What that means for sequencers, RPC providers and smart contract developers is where the real story sits.

For about sixteen months, Base's fastest blocks were only promises. Since November 5, they are the ledger itself.

Denim went live on Base mainnet on November 5, after activating on Sepolia on October 21.

According to the upgrade page, the chain now produces five complete canonical blocks every second instead of one every two seconds. Flashblocks, the preconfirmation layer that ran alongside the two-second blocks since July 2025, is retired.

In a recent development, most coverage stopped at the speed figure. The sharper question is what separates a canonical block from a preconfirmation, because that gap decides what breaks and what improves for anyone building on the chain.

Those updates were the sequencer's early word on what the next block would contain. They were previews of pending state, and nothing in them had its own hash, state root or receipts until the two-second block was sealed. Developers therefore had to keep an early execution result mentally separate from a settled transaction.

Sources indicate that denim turns the 200ms unit into the real thing. Under Base's 200ms Native Blocks specification, every block carries its own number, hash, state root, receipts and forkchoice updates, and moves through the unsafe, safe and finalized stages like any other block.

The sequencer's job gets heavier and stricter. Instead of streaming fragments of a larger block, it has to build and execute a full block for every 200ms slot. The header keeps its timestamp in whole seconds, so Denim adds a metadata transaction, the BaseTime deposit, placed second in every block. It supplies the sub-second portion: 0, 200, 400, 600 or 800 milliseconds.

It has been revealed that timing rules are tight. Slots can't be skipped, and each block's full timestamp must land exactly 200ms after its parent's. That timestamp comes from a schedule tied to the Denim activation and the block number, not from the sequencer's clock, so wall-clock time only determines when a build begins. Once execution finishes, the client rejects any block that breaks the 200ms progression.

This removes a layer of ambiguity. A preconfirmation was only as strong as the sequencer's word, while a canonical block can be validated, replayed and challenged by any node running the same derivation rules.

Recent findings suggest that app developers face the biggest practical shift. Flashblocks streams ended at activation, so anything built on newFlashblocks, pendingLogs or the pending block tag has to move to canonical subscriptions like newHeads and logs. The migration guide lists the API changes required.

The seconds-based timestamp field stays as it was for compatibility. Block, header, transaction, log and receipt responses now include optional millisecond fields, timestampMs and blockTimestampMs, derived from authenticated BaseTime data. They are left out when that data has been pruned or is unavailable. One tooling detail deserves attention: the spec warns that the plain Alloy AnyRpcHeader type drops unknown fields, so anyone who needs millisecond timestamps must use a different type.

Industry observers note that node providers will see heavier traffic too. Dwellir's analysis notes that any service doing work on every block now does it ten times as often. Five fetches a second replace one every two seconds. Denim improves latency without adding capacity, so infrastructure bills are likely to climb.

Finality hasn't gone away either. Faster production doesn't erase the confirmation policy an application picks, and each 200ms block still passes through the same unsafe, safe and finalized stages. Bridges and exchanges that wait for a specific stage before crediting funds may need to rethink how many blocks they wait for, since a block count no longer equals the same stretch of time.

It has been revealed that this is the area that deserves the most urgent attention. Base's spec warns that block.number now advances ten times faster in real time, while block.timestamp still ticks in whole seconds. A contract that treats a block count as a duration will see that duration collapse to a tenth of what its authors intended.

The affected patterns are common ones. Timelocks and cooldowns measured in blocks expire in a tenth of the time. Vesting and emission schedules run ten times faster. Per-block rate limits reset five times a second instead of once every two seconds, which lifts the effective per-second limit tenfold. Governance voting windows set in blocks shrink the same way. Uniswap V3-style TWAP oracles stay accurate, but a fixed observation cardinality now covers less wall-clock history, so long lookbacks can revert sooner.

Industry observers note that contracts built on block.timestamp are unaffected. Where a block count can be adjusted through governance, teams blueprint to divide it by ten. Where it is hardcoded into an immutable contract, the spec says it can't be retuned after activation, which leaves migration as the only fix. Denim also tightens transfer rules for Base's B20 token standard, and transfers to a token's own address now revert.

According to recent reports, the coming weeks will show how much of this stays theoretical. Three things are worth tracking: whether any immutable contract with block-count logic misbehaves, how providers cope with the jump in per-block requests, and whether apps built around Flashblocks have fully moved over.

It has been revealed that denim looks like a cleaner design than the layer it replaced. A preview mechanism gives way to a block anyone can verify, and developers pay for it with a real migration. Speed grabbed the headlines, but the lasting change is that Base's sub-second confirmations now stand on the same footing as the chain's ordinary blocks.

Considering the history of the transferred funds, the move has sparked speculation that the hacker might already be preparing to spend the stolen funds, further sabotaging Binance’s chances of full recovery.

However, it is key to note that there is no evidence that the attacker has sold the Ethereum, as the receiving wallet has not been identified.

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 17, 2026 at 6:36 pmNovember 17, 2026 at 6:36 pm.

Jeff Bezos has a space firm, a newspaper, an AI startup that’s raised $14.5 billion and, apparently, a seat in the room when Amazon decides who gets a license to kill.

Speaking Tuesday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event, the Amazon founder said he was “heavily involved” in the casting of Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond, a pick Amazon MGM Studios announced Monday.

Amazon got a 50% stake in the Bond franchise when it acquired MGM for $8.5 billion in 2022, then took creative control last year in a joint venture with longtime producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson.

Bezos said a large initial pool of would-be Bonds was narrowed to five finalists, who then did “real old-fashioned screen tests”: three scenes apiece, in full costume on real sets with other actors.

The other finalists were Nicholas Hoult, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Callum Turner, according to The New York Times, which reported that the tests took place in London in late October.

Bezos noted the decision-makers got together Friday and spent a couple of hours reviewing the screen tests before settling on Pattinson.

In a recent development, “By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing,” Bezos said. “But there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances.” He said the group, including director Denis Villeneuve, reached a quick consensus. It was “kind of immediately undebated.”.

Bezos admitted that the group was initially “slightly biased” against Pattinson because he’s already so famous.

“We sort of thought, you know, maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown,” he remarked. “But in the screen tests, it was so obvious he is James Bond.”.
